q: What is included in an SEO service plan?
a: A plan starts with site and search analysis, then prioritises technical fixes, relevant pages, content improvements and measurement. The exact deliverables depend on the site's platform, market and business goals.

q: Do I need an SEO audit before ongoing work?
a: A focused audit gives you a baseline and reveals whether crawlability, content gaps or conversion issues need attention first. It can be a standalone project or the first phase of ongoing SEO.

q: What is the difference between on-page and technical SEO?
a: On-page SEO improves a page's content, headings, intent and internal links. Technical SEO addresses crawling, indexing, rendering, site architecture and performance. Both support useful search pages.

q: Can you work with an existing developer or content team?
a: Yes. SEO recommendations can be written as developer-ready tickets and writer-ready briefs, with priorities and acceptance checks so the team can implement them clearly.

q: How soon can SEO services improve rankings?
a: There is no fixed timeline. Existing pages with clear issues may improve after fixes are crawled, while competitive topics often need months of content and authority work.

q: Which tools are useful for an SEO project?
a: Google Search Console and analytics are the starting point. Crawlers, keyword tools and server logs can add detail where the site's size and technical setup justify them.

q: Is SEO worth it for a small business?
a: It can be when customers search for your services and you can serve those searches well. Local profiles, service pages, reviews and clear contact paths often matter more than publishing many generic articles.

q: How do we start an SEO project?
a: Share your website, target market and business goal. The next step is to review the existing search visibility and agree on the highest-value problem to solve first.
